newsitem.title: USA: Rights group intervenes over Iranian academic.
newsitem.headline: Rights group intervenes over Iranian academic.

text.p: A U.S. human rights group accused the Iranian government on Tuesday of harassment and arbitrary assaults on the basic civil and political rights of one of the country's leading scholars.

In an open letter to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the New York-based Human Rights Watch said Abdol Karim Soroush, a proponent of religious reform in Iran, had been effectively banned from teaching since last year and recently had also been prohibited from travelling abroad to attend international academic conferences.

The letter, a copy of which was also sent to Rafsanjani's successor Mohammad Khatami who takes over next month, said Soroush's passport had been confiscated and he had been prevented from attending academic seminars to which he was invited in Germany, Malaysia and, most recently, Britain.
Soroush had recently been threatened by an Information (intelligence) Ministry official with possible imprisonment if he continued to express views critical of the Iranian government, the group said.
"Dr Soroush is one of the boldest thinkers in Iran today and he has a considerable international following," said Joseph Saunders, HRW academic freedom specialist.
"The government's treatment of Dr Soroush will be an important indicator of whether the new government is genuinely committed to greater openness in Iranian society."
